structured_output.what_is_happening: A copycat "American Reserved Oil Supply" (AROS) token, 19 minutes old at detection. It rides a very large AROS narrative: several same-ticker coins sit at $360M-$900M market cap. This one is not a pump.fun mint (no 'pump' suffix, platform unknown). Its PumpSwap pool was created 3 seconds after the token itself, seeded with more liquidity (~$42k) than the token's market cap (~$27k), and 100% of the LP is unlocked. It shows 1,620 unique buyers against 99 unique sellers and $315k of volume in about 20 minutes. Two other non-pump AROS clones launched within the last ~1.7 hours already show $0 liquidity, and one of them did $245k of 1h volume before dying. That matches a serial pattern: seed the LP, draw buyers, pull the LP.

narrative.description: AROS / American Reserved Oil Supply is an already mega-successful narrative, with multiple tokens at hundreds of millions in market cap. This token is a late derivative clone of it.
narrative.why_spreading: Spillover from the huge AROS names, as traders scan for cheap same-name tickers. It is not a new story, and the canonical tokens have already captured it.

token_connection.why_this_token: Same name and ticker only. It has no socials, website or DexScreener profile, and nothing ties it to the canonical AROS.
token_connection.competing_tokens: At least 8 live AROS tokens, from $3.6M to $900M market cap, plus 2 recent same-name non-pump clones that already show zero liquidity (rugged).

authenticity.evidence: The buyer count is broad (1,620 unique buyers, top10 ~8-11%, 8 bundler wallets holding only ~2%), which is consistent with real clone-hunting retail. But the 16:1 buyer-to-seller ratio, a dev-seeded pool with liquidity above market cap, and an identical pattern on clones that already rugged suggest the setup is engineered to attract buyers before the LP is pulled.
authenticity.uncertainty: Without X data I can't tell whether callers pushed this clone. Some buyers may be bots that hunt copycats.

structural_risks: 100% of LP is unlocked, and the creator can remove liquidity at any time
Pool was created manually outside the pump.fun curve (non-pump mint, unknown platform)
Liquidity is above market cap, i.e. the dev seeded the pool, which is a classic LP-pull setup
Two sibling same-name clones already at $0 liquidity within the last ~2 hours

structured_output.counterargument: Demand is genuinely broad: 1,620 unique buyers, low holder concentration, no snipers and very few bundlers. The AROS narrative is so hot that a $27k clone could go 2-3x quickly on overflow flow before any pull. If the dev keeps the LP in to farm fees, or waits for a larger pool, the price could double well within the entry window.
unknowns: Whether the creator (status 'creator_close') still controls the LP tokens
Whether the rugged sibling clones share this deployer
Whether the buyers are copy-bots or retail
Whether X or call channels are promoting this contract

structured_output.thesis: This is a non-canonical AROS clone in a manually seeded pool with fully unlocked LP, liquidity above market cap, and sibling clones that already rugged. Strong short-term buying doesn't make up for a high chance the LP gets pulled within hours. Rank it low.
